title: fetch
text:
labdata.fetch(spec_text, refresh=False, cfg=None)
Get a local path to a result file, fetching it if it is not cached.



spec_text : str

A spec of the form [owner/]repo:path[@version]. Without a version, the latest is used.

refresh : bool = False

Rescan the repositories before resolving the spec.

cfg : Optional[Config] = None

Settings. Defaults to labdata.config.Config.load.






 : Path

Path of the file in the local cache, ready to pass to a reader.






: ValueError

If spec_text cannot be parsed.

: LookupError

If the spec matches no entry, several entries, or no version.

: FileNotFoundError

If the file is held in Git LFS and its content has not been fetched into the repository.





Read a result file from another project into a notebook:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv(fetch("munch-group/xwas:hits.csv@e4f5a6b"))

title: discover_repos
text:
labdata.gitutil.discover_repos(roots, depth=2)
Find git working trees under a set of root directories.
A root that is itself a working tree is returned directly; otherwise its subdirectories are searched. Descent stops at each working tree, so nested repositories such as submodules are not reported separately.



roots : Iterable[Union[str, Path]]

Directories to search. ~ is expanded. Roots that do not exist are skipped silently.

depth : int = 2

How many levels below each root to search.






 : List[Path]

Absolute paths of the working trees found, without duplicates.





discover_repos(["~/github-backup/munch-group"], depth=1)

title: materialize
text:
labdata.core.materialize(entry, version)
Place one version of a result file in the cache and return its path.
Content already cached is not fetched again, which is why an unchanged file costs nothing across versions and repositories. Git LFS content is taken from the repository’s own object store.



entry : Entry

Entry the version belongs to.

version : Version

Version to materialize.






 : Path

Readable path of the cached content, under <cache>/files/<repo>/<version>/<name>.






: FileNotFoundError

If the content is held in Git LFS and has not been fetched. The message names the git lfs fetch command to run.

Stream the content of a blob to a file.
Git writes straight into dest, so peak memory does not grow with the size of the file.



repo : Path

Working tree holding the blob.

blob_sha : str

Blob sha to read.

dest : Path

File to write. It is removed again if git fails.






: GitError

If git cannot read the blob.

labdata.Config(
    roots=(lambda: ['~'])(),
    depth=2,
    results_dirs=(lambda: ['results'])(),
    include=(lambda: list(DEFAULT_INCLUDE))(),
    exclude=(lambda: list(DEFAULT_EXCLUDE))(),
    min_bytes=0,
    max_bytes=0,
)
Settings controlling which files are cataloged.



roots : List[str]

Directories searched for git working trees. ~ is expanded.

depth : int

How many levels below each root to search.

results_dirs : List[str]

Directories within a repository holding published result files. Matching is case-insensitive, so a repository that committed Results/ is found as well.

include : List[str]

File name patterns to catalog.

exclude : List[str]

File name patterns to skip, applied before include.

min_bytes : int

Skip files smaller than this. Zero disables the check.

max_bytes : int

Skip files larger than this. Zero disables the check.





cfg = Config(roots=["~/github-backup/munch-group"], depth=1)
entries = build(cfg)

title: Version
text:
labdata.Version(sha, short, date, subject, blob, size, lfs_oid=None, tags=())
One commit in which a result file changed.
A version is defined by a commit, not by a repository tag. Analysis repos are rarely tagged, whereas every change to a result file is a commit, so commits give a version key that exists without extra discipline. Tags, when present, are carried in tags and can be used to address a version, but they never define one.



sha : str

Full sha of the commit in which the file last changed.

short : str

Abbreviated commit sha. This is the user-facing version key.

date : str

Committer date in ISO-8601 format.

subject : str

Subject line of the commit.

blob : str

Git blob sha of the file at this commit. This is a hash of the file content, and is used as the cache key.

size : int

Size of the file in bytes, resolved through Git LFS pointers so that it is the size of the real content rather than of the pointer.

lfs_oid : Optional[str]

The sha256 object id when the file is stored in Git LFS, else None.

tags : Tuple[str, …]

Any tags pointing at this commit.

title: tracked_blobs
text:
labdata.gitutil.tracked_blobs(repo, subdir)
List files tracked at HEAD under a directory, with blob shas and sizes.
Only tracked files are reported, so untracked scratch output sitting in a results directory is invisible to the catalog: committing a file is the act of publishing it. Symbolic links are skipped.



repo : Path

Working tree to inspect.

subdir : str

Pathspec limiting the listing, for example :(icase)results.






 : Dict[str, Tuple[str, int]]

A mapping of repository-relative path to (blob_sha, size). Sizes are those of the stored blob, so a Git LFS pointer reports the size of the pointer; use labdata.gitutil.parse_lfs_pointer to resolve it.
